author: Forbes
description:
Bipartisan lawmakers are demanding a federal investigation into billionaire Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang—and one is demanding his resignation—following revelations of an extramarital affair with an executive suspected of ties to Chinese intelligence.

Sen. Kevin Cramer (R-N.D.) has called on Huang to resign his post as top executive of the country’s largest AI chipmaker, telling Politico late Tuesday that “the potential for extortion is so tremendous.”

Cramer, who sits on the Senate Banking Committee, said Huang’s place at Nvidia is a “security risk” after the details of his affair were exposed, and President Donald Trump earlier this week confirmed the FBI is looking into the situation.

description:
Engineered from two algae-derived polysaccharides, TraumaGel is injected directly into severe lacerations and bullet wounds to stop life-threatening hemorrhages on contact. Today, Cresilon operates as the only bio-manufacturing facility in New York City, with over 100 employees and its products are deployed in more than 250 national trauma systems.

Cofounder and CEO Joe Landolina breaks down the journey from a college dorm room concept to an FDA-cleared device transforming emergency trauma response.

author: Forbes
description:
Jim Higdon is planning for the best Black Friday of his life. It may also be the last. Inside Cornbread Hemp’s 25,000-square-foot gummy factory in Louisville, Kentucky, the lines are running full and the warehouse is filling up for the biggest sales day of the year. Two weeks after that, on December 11, a federal ban on hemp-derived THC takes effect. If it holds, Cornbread’s record $65 million in revenue this year ends, and so does most of the $38.5 billion industry around it, a market that now outsells legal marijuana. Higdon has 106 employees, a personally guaranteed loan on the facility expansion, and a month to make as much money as possible.
